BiblicalUsage: Jacob's sons mourned their father seven days with a great and sore lamentation, the Jews in every province mourned with fasting and weeping and wailing, and Amos says the Lord will call the husbandman to mourning and those skilful of lamentation to wailing. The word is the lament itself, and Scripture gives it its own skilled mourners.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that lamentation is a holy work: seven days for a father, wailing in every province, and men skilled in lamentation called to mourn, because grief that is not mourned turns bitter. Grief that is not mourned turns bitter, so Scripture gives it its own skilled mourners.
